# GEO report: quay-store **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 40/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points). How it's calculated: low = 12 ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. High = (12 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. Nothing was unknown, so both numbers are 48. The score is capped at 40 because of a blocker. `robots.txt` blocks Googlebot from the whole site (GEO-009). Two things drag the score down. Google is told to stay away from the whole site, and the pages only appear after JavaScript runs. Both are quick to fix. All results are read from code, not from a running site. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking Googlebot in robots.txt - **Why it matters:** Googlebot is told not to read any page, including the pages your sitemap and menu point to. Google can't read your pages while this stays. - **Where:** `static/robots.txt:4-5` - **What the code says:** `User-agent: Googlebot` / `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 72/100 (Good). GEO-009 and GEO-014 both become clear, and the cap lifts. ### 2. Make pages render on the server - **Why it matters:** Many crawlers read only the first HTML the server sends. With server rendering off, they see an empty `
` and none of your headings, text or menu links. - **Where:** `src/routes/+layout.ts:1` - **What the code says:** `export const ssr = false;` - **Size:** Small. Remove the line, or set it to `true`, and check that nothing needs the browser at load time. - **Score after this:** 84/100 (with item 1 applied). ### 3. Set the page language and fill the empty description - **Why it matters:** The `lang` attribute tells machines which language the site is in. The Shop page's empty description gives them nothing to show about that page. - **Where:** `src/app.html:2` and `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:3` - **What the code says:** `` and `` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 92/100 (with items 1 and 2 applied). This adds `lang="en"` and a real Shop description. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and a sensible size | Clear | Not run | `static/robots.txt`: valid lines, tiny file | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers can reach the site | Problem | Not run | `static/robots.txt:4-5` Googlebot `Disallow: /`. Site-wide, so 0 of 3 points. Assumed you want to be found, because there's no `geo.config.json` | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `/` and `/shop` are blocked for Googlebot by `robots.txt`. `/search` is `noindex` on purpose, isn't in the sitemap or menu, and is left out | | GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your domain | Clear | Not run | `src/routes/+page.svelte:4`, `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:4`. The domain is `quay.example`, matching the sitemap and `robots.txt` | | GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `src/routes/+layout.ts:1` `ssr = false`, with an empty body shell in `src/app.html:8` | | GEO-004 | Structured data is valid | Problem | Not run | `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:5`. The `Product` has only `name`. It lacks `offers`, `review` or `aggregateRating`, one of which Google needs for a product. Found on 1 of 1 routes | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is linked from robots.txt | Clear | Not run | `static/sitemap.xml`, `static/robots.txt:7` | | GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` | Problem | Not run | `src/app.html:2` has no `lang`, which hits every route. `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:3` has an empty description | | GEO-016 | Key pages are reachable by normal links | Clear | Not run | `src/routes/+layout.svelte:5` has ``. Whether these links reach crawlers depends on GEO-003 | | GEO-017 | No page-wide snippet blocking | Clear | Not run | None found. `data-nosnippet` on one element (`+layout.svelte:7`) is a deliberate choice | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | Read the layout and 3 pages: no images, links have text, titles present | | GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present. It's optional and not scored | | GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | No app | ## Other problems found - **The Shop page's structured data is only added in the browser.** It's written with `{@html …}` inside `` at `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:5`, and server rendering is off, so it isn't in the server HTML. It will start working once item 2 is done. - Nothing else found. ## Worth considering - **Make the delivery and shipping promise something a machine can read:** `src/routes/+page.svelte:7` has `

Marine parts, shipped next day

`. The only delivery terms are in a `data-nosnippet` block (`src/routes/+layout.svelte:7`: `Free delivery over £50.`). Keep that block as it is, since hiding it from snippets looks deliberate. A visible shipping page would let the "next day" claim be backed up in text. - **Give each product its own page:** `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:9` has `

Bilge pumps, cleats and rope.

`. Each item could have its own address, with a name, price and description. Then the `Product` data could describe real items. - **Link from the home page to the products:** `src/routes/+page.svelte:7` has only a heading, so the home page links onward only through the menu. A short intro with links to the categories might help readers and crawlers. - **Add `viewport` to the head:** `src/app.html:4` has `` and nothing for viewport. This affects how the page is read on phones. - **Add `
` around the page content:** `src/routes/+layout.svelte:6` has `{@render children()}` outside any landmark. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. To check, run `geopilot logs `, which compares real crawler requests with their published addresses. - **Real status codes and headers:** whether `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml` and the pages answer 200, and whether the host adds an `X-Robots-Tag` header. A live scan with your URL would settle these. - **The domain:** I took `quay.example` from the sitemap and `robots.txt`. It looks like a placeholder, so confirm the real production domain. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site, because there's no `geo.config.json`. - `/search` being `noindex` is intended. - The sampled routes were `/`, `/shop` and `/search`, which are all the routes. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-009`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
